predictions.title: Transformer-only inference ASICs gain a first-class serving-stack backend by H1 2027
predictions.body: Etched came out of stealth on July 1 with a working transformer-specialized inference ASIC on TSMC's N4P, more than $1 billion in customer contracts signed before the part has shipped, and an architecture that hard-wires the transformer into silicon and shares one low-latency memory pool across the whole scale-up domain over a proprietary interconnect. The load-bearing move is not the funding but the architectural bet: dropping the training-oriented generality of a GPU to buy density on model serving, the workload that now dominates production spend. A fixed-function part only pays off if real model traffic can reach it without a bespoke integration for every deployment, and today the mainstream serving runtimes, vLLM, SGLang, and TensorRT-LLM class stacks, are built around CUDA-style general accelerators with paged-attention and continuous-batching schedulers assuming a programmable GPU underneath. An order book measured in billions before first shipment is exactly the demand signal that pulls a serving stack to add a non-GPU, fixed-function transformer backend as a supported target rather than a fork. This also rhymes with the adjacent move of a rival accelerator vendor acquiring a CUDA-agnostic inference compiler to route models onto non-NVIDIA parts. Expect at least one mainstream open-source or hyperscaler-managed serving stack to expose a transformer-ASIC or comparable fixed-function inference backend as a documented, first-class deployment path, with the same model-definition and API surface a GPU target already gets, so that pointing production traffic at fixed-function silicon stops requiring a custom stack. The coupling is that a billion-dollar pre-ship order book turns backend generality from the ASIC vendor's private problem into a feature the serving layer ships.

reasoning.because: Etched left stealth with a working transformer-only inference ASIC and $1B+ in pre-ship contracts
reasoning.given: Mainstream serving runtimes assume programmable GPUs; a billion-dollar order book pulls in a fixed-function backend
reasoning.so_that: A mainstream serving stack exposes a transformer-ASIC fixed-function backend as a documented first-class deployment path
reasoning.landing: by H1 2027; a serving runtime or managed stack lists a fixed-function transformer-ASIC backend
reasoning.plain_language: A chip that only runs transformers already has huge orders, so the software that serves AI models will add built-in support for that kind of chip.

predictions.summary: Etched left stealth with a working transformer-only inference ASIC and over $1B in contracts before shipping, betting on fixed-function density over GPU generality. Since mainstream serving runtimes assume programmable GPUs, expect at least one to expose a transformer-ASIC fixed-function backend as a first-class deployment path by H1 2027.

predictions.title: Inference-ASIC challenger anchors a raise on a $1B+ order book by Q4 2027
predictions.body: Etched's stealth exit on July 1 priced a transformer-only inference ASIC on a metric that barely existed a year ago: not shipped revenue, not even a working part alone, but more than $1 billion in signed customer contracts for a chip that has not yet shipped, disclosed alongside $800 million raised and a $5 billion post-money valuation set in its December round. The order book is doing the valuation work. A forward purchase commitment measured in billions, backed by a fabricated N4P part in hand and a running test line, lets a pre-revenue challenger clear a valuation that shipped-revenue comparables would take years to justify, and it hands investors a demand-side underwrite that a benchmark deck cannot. This is a commercial template, not a one-off: the non-NVIDIA serving field is crowded with parts still ahead of first shipment, and every one of them faces the same problem of proving that generality-for-density is a demand thesis rather than an engineering bet. The cleanest way to prove it, now demonstrated, is to convert design-win intent into a disclosed contracted backlog and lead with that number. Expect a second inference-silicon challenger beyond Etched to close a round or set a valuation anchored on a disclosed pre-shipment contracted order book crossing the billion-dollar mark, with the backlog figure, not a shipped-units or run-rate number, cited as the headline commercial proof. The structural read is that the inference-accelerator category is being financed against forward purchase commitments the way capital-intensive infrastructure has long been, so the order book becomes the instrument that clears the pre-shipment valuation gap, and disclosing one becomes a competitive necessity rather than a flourish.

reasoning.because: Etched disclosed >$1B in signed contracts for an unshipped inference ASIC at a $5B valuation
reasoning.given: Rival non-NVIDIA serving parts still pre-shipment must prove density-for-generality is real demand
reasoning.so_that: A second inference-silicon challenger anchors a raise or valuation on a disclosed >$1B pre-shipment order book
reasoning.landing: by Q4 2027; a second vendor leads with a $1B+ contracted backlog
reasoning.plain_language: A chip startup was valued on $1B of orders for a chip it has not shipped, so a rival will likely raise the same way.

predictions.summary: Etched exited stealth pricing a transformer-only inference ASIC on over $1B in signed contracts for a chip that has not shipped. The pre-shipment order book, not shipped revenue, clears its valuation, so expect a second inference-silicon challenger to anchor a raise on a $1B+ backlog by Q4 2027.

predictions.title: Companion-agent memory guardrails become binding rules in a second major market by Q4 2027
predictions.body: China's Interim Measures for the Administration of AI Anthropomorphic Interaction Services, issued in April 2026 and taking effect July 15, 2026, became the first live regime to treat persistent-identity emotional-companion agents as a regulated product surface, and ByteDance's Doubao and Alibaba's Qwen resolved compliance over the July 3-6 weekend by switching the features off rather than redesigning them. Qwen is disabling humanlike interactive and user-created agents on July 10 and broader agent services on July 15, while Doubao pulls its agent feature July 15 and gives users until October 15 to export data before it is unrecoverable. The load-bearing detail is the shape of the mandate, not the shutdown: the rules require anti-addiction systems, in-session usage notifications, and instant-exit mechanisms, and they carve out customer-service, knowledge-Q&A, workplace, and education tools that lack the sustained emotional-companion framing. That draws a precise, copyable regulatory line around exactly the capabilities the agent-harness field has been racing to add, long-horizon memory and a consistent cross-session persona, and it does so in enforceable statute with a hard effective date rather than a consultation draft. The same consumer-harm concerns that motivated it, minor safety, dependency, and disclosure of machine identity, are already live in EU AI Act transparency obligations, in US state proposals on companion chatbots, and in ongoing scrutiny of youth-facing AI companions elsewhere. Expect a second major jurisdiction to convert that concern into a binding instrument, a statute, enacted rule, or enforceable code, that imposes companion-specific guardrails on emotional-companion or persistent-memory agents: mandated machine-identity disclosure, anti-addiction or usage-limit controls, and a data-export-or-deletion path on shutdown, tracking the same emotional-companion scope carve-out China drew. The coupling is that a live enforced template plus overlapping consumer-protection pressure turns companion-AI memory and persona from a product-design choice into a regulated surface in more than one market, and vendors keep resolving the tension by withdrawal or scope-narrowing rather than by building compliant persistence.

reasoning.because: China's April 2026 anthropomorphic-AI rules take effect July 15; Doubao and Qwen pulled companion agents to comply
reasoning.given: Rules mandate anti-addiction, usage alerts, instant-exit and scope out non-companion tools; EU/US echo the concern
reasoning.so_that: A second major jurisdiction enacts a binding instrument imposing companion-specific memory, disclosure and exit guardrails
reasoning.landing: by Q4 2027, a second market enacts binding companion-AI guardrails on persistent-memory agents
reasoning.plain_language: China now legally limits AI friend apps that remember you, so another big country will likely pass its own rules on them soon.

predictions.summary: China's Interim Measures on AI anthropomorphic interaction take effect July 15, 2026, and ByteDance's Doubao and Alibaba's Qwen withdrew persistent-memory companion agents rather than redesign them to meet anti-addiction, usage-alert, and instant-exit mandates. With EU and US consumer-protection pressure echoing the same concern, expect a second major jurisdiction to enact binding companion-AI guardrails on emotional-companion or persistent-memory agents by Q4 2027.
